steps.action: Write the design record in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md. Read the approved plan first (context path): its sections `Design`, `Invariants`, `Rejected` and `Stage 0` are the content. (1) Add a new `## Garbage collection` section directly before `## Rejected designs`. It must state: s3armor writes no sidecar objects, so a delete or an overwrite leaves no garbage and no bucket walk is necessary; the inventory of garbage sources (finished sessions in RAM, orphaned backend multipart uploads from a restart, from the cap race in handle_create, and from a failed sweeper abort, plus two sources that stay uncollected on purpose: `s3a-check-*` and `s3a-bench-*` objects after a killed run, and new versions from `rewrap` or `rebind` on a versioned bucket); collector 1 (`Session::finish` releases the DEK, parts and tails at Complete, and `Sessions::make_room` removes the finished session with the oldest activity when the node is at the cap); collector 2 (the lifecycle rule of the backend that aborts incomplete multipart uploads, made visible by a read-only `s3armor check` probe, with the MinIO exception: MinIO ignores that rule field and removes stale uploads on its own, `api stale_uploads_expiry`, default 24 h); the invariants from the plan, with the rule that garbage collection never deletes an object version because versioning is the rollback mitigation; the known limit (at the cap, a finished session can be removed before its client retries Complete, and that retry then gets NoSuchUpload). (2) Add the rejected designs from the plan to `## Rejected designs`, each with its reason: the `s3armor gc` subcommand (and the note that a later version must use idle time from the newest part LastModified of ListParts, because an age filter on Initiated can abort a slow upload that is still live), backend garbage collection inside `serve`, a second clock for finished sessions, a second map for finished sessions, a timer wheel or heap for expiry. (3) Correct the sentences that the code change makes false: the Zeroization section near line 354 (`exactly three sites` becomes four sites: the session DEK is zeroized at Complete and on Drop) and the dependency table row near line 507; the session state sentence near lines 256-258 (a finished session keeps only the cached response); the Complete retry text near lines 290-292 and the section `Multipart sessions are RAM, single instance` near lines 903-906 (add the release at Complete and the removal at the cap). (4) Add the new probe to the probe list of the section `Backend conformance check` near lines 649-668: it reads the lifecycle configuration of the bucket, it writes nothing, and it gives Warn, never Fail. Match the style, heading depth and line width of the file. Do not change any other section.

steps.action: Fix the lifetime of finished multipart sessions. Read the approved plan first (context path), section `Collector 1`. Work test-first: write the tests, run them, see them fail, then write the code. Tests, in the existing `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` of crates/s3armor/src/mpu.rs: `finish_releases_the_dek_parts_and_tails` (after `finish`, `dek` is None, `parts` and `tails` are empty, `completed` is Some), `record_part_on_a_finished_session_changes_nothing` (after `finish`, `Session::record_part` with a tail leaves `parts` and `tails` empty), `make_room_at_the_cap_evicts_the_oldest_finished_session` (fill to MAX_SESSIONS with two finished sessions of different `last_activity`; `make_room` returns true, the older finished session is gone, the newer one and all open sessions stay), `make_room_at_the_cap_with_no_finished_session_rejects` (fill to MAX_SESSIONS with open sessions; `make_room` returns false and the length does not change). One integration test in crates/s3armor/tests/integration_mpu.rs, `upload_part_after_complete_is_no_such_upload`, built from the existing helpers `setup`, `create_upload`, `upload_one`, `complete`: an UploadPart after a successful Complete gives the S3 error code NoSuchUpload. This test is a contract pin; it passes before and after the change. Code in crates/s3armor/src/mpu.rs: (a) `Session.dek` becomes `Option<[u8; 32]>`; `Session::new` keeps its signature and stores `Some(dek)`; the `Drop` impl still calls `self.dek.zeroize()`. (b) `pub fn finish(&mut self, cached: CachedComplete)`: zeroize the DEK (this leaves None), clear `parts` and `tails`, set `completed`, call `touch()`. (c) `pub fn record_part(&mut self, part_number: u32, pt_len: u64, etag: String, ct: Option<Bytes>)`: return at once when `completed.is_some()`; else do what the body of the free function `record_part` in intercept/mpu.rs does today (insert the PartRecord, apply the tail rule, touch). (d) `pub fn make_room(&self) -> bool` on `Sessions`: true when `len() < MAX_SESSIONS`; at the cap, find the key of the finished session with the oldest `last_activity`, end the iterator, then remove that key and return true; return false when no finished session exists. Never call `remove` while a DashMap iterator or Ref is alive: that deadlocks. Follow the collect-then-remove pattern of `take_expired`. Add a `ponytail:` comment: O(MAX_SESSIONS) scan, only at the cap; an ordered index is the upgrade path if the cap grows past about 10000. (e) `Sessions::create` calls `make_room` in place of the raw length comparison, and still accepts a key that already exists. Code in crates/s3armor/src/intercept/mpu.rs: the pre-check at the top of `handle_create` calls `state.sessions.make_room()` in place of the length comparison; `handle_upload_part` and `snapshot_for_complete` map a `None` DEK to `S3Error::no_such_upload(&upload_id)` with `ok_or_else` (no unwrap, no expect, no indexing); the free function `record_part` becomes a delegate to `Session::record_part`; `complete_upload` calls `entry.finish(CachedComplete { .. })` on success in place of the two assignments, and its failure branch stays as it is. Refresh the doc comments that the change makes false: the module comment and the comments on `CachedComplete` and `MAX_SESSIONS` in mpu.rs, and the comments near the cap race and above `handle_complete` in intercept/mpu.rs. Do not change `expired`, `take_expired`, the sweeper, or any existing test.

steps.action: Add a read-only lifecycle probe to crates/s3armor/src/tools/check.rs. Read the approved plan first (context path), section `Collector 2`. Work test-first. (a) A pure function `fn classify_lifecycle(status: u16, server: Option<&str>, body: &[u8]) -> Status`, no network. Rules, in this order: the `server` value contains `MinIO` (ASCII case-insensitive) gives `Status::Ok`; status 200 and the body has a `Rule` whose `Status` text is `Enabled` and which has an `AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload` element gives `Status::Ok`; status 200 with no such rule (this includes a rule that has the element but is `Disabled`) gives `Status::Warn`; status 404 gives `Status::Warn` (no lifecycle configuration); status 403 gives `Status::Warn` and the text names the permission `s3:GetLifecycleConfiguration`; any other status gives `Status::Warn` with the text that the lifecycle configuration cannot be read and the status number. Never `Status::Fail`. The Warn texts for a missing rule say that orphaned multipart parts stay billed until a rule aborts incomplete multipart uploads. Parse rule by rule with `quick_xml` events, as crates/s3armor/src/tools/list.rs does; a substring search is wrong because it accepts a Disabled rule. (b) The first `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` of this file, with these seven tests: `a_minio_server_header_is_ok`, `an_enabled_abort_rule_is_ok`, `a_disabled_abort_rule_warns`, `a_lifecycle_with_no_abort_rule_warns`, `a_missing_lifecycle_configuration_warns`, `a_forbidden_lifecycle_read_warns_and_names_the_permission`, `an_unexpected_status_warns`. `Status` has no PartialEq; use `matches!` in the tests, do not add derives that the code does not need. (c) An async probe `lifecycle_abort_rule_probe(state, backend, bucket) -> Probe` that sends `GET /{bucket}` with the query `lifecycle` through `forward` with an empty body, reads the `server` response header with the existing `header_owned` and `to_pairs`, collects the body, and calls `classify_lifecycle`. A transport error gives `Status::Warn` with the error text. The probe writes nothing to the bucket. (d) Append the probe to the `vec!` in `check()`, after `multipart_small_final_part_probe`. The lint policy denies unwrap, expect and indexing outside tests. Do not change any other probe.
